content.title: About
content.content: Pocky is a Japanese snack consisting of thin biscuit sticks coated with a layer of chocolate or other flavored glazes. It was first introduced in 1966 and quickly became popular both in Japan and worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original flavor was chocolate, but today the range includes strawberry, green tea, caramel, and many more.
In Japan Pocky is often served as a sweet stick snack alongside tea.
The name “Pocky” is derived from the English word “pocket,” hinting at its convenient portability.
In 2014 a “Create Your Own Pocky” contest was launched in the US, allowing consumers to propose new flavors.
Pocky frequently appears in photos and memes because of its bright packaging.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Contains carbohydrates that provide quick energy.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: The biscuit and coating supply a modest amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Calcium from chocolate coating
items.content: Milk chocolate variants contain calcium, beneficial for bones.

items.title: Antioxidants in cocoa
items.content: Dark chocolate versions are rich in flavonoids, which may support heart health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The biscuit is made with wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Most flavors contain a high amount of sugar, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Chocolate varieties often contain milk, posing a risk for those allergic to dairy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pocky is calorie‑dense, and large portions can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pocky is designed to be eaten by hand, breaking off sticks from the package. They can be used as a topping for desserts, mixed into ice cream, yogurt, or baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer shelf life, keep in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate coating from melting.
